hints.content: There are $3\dfrac{2}{5}$ seconds between the time $-3\dfrac{2}{5}$ seconds and $0$ seconds.

The video plays $25$ frames per second.

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}25\,\dfrac{\text{frames}}{\text{s}} \times 3\dfrac{2}{5} \,\text{s}\\\\
&=25\,\dfrac{\text{frames}}{\cancel{\text{s}}} \times \dfrac{17}{5} \,\cancel{\text{s}}\\\\
&=85\,\text{frames}
\end{align}$

The video played $85$ frames between those times. How many frames played before that set of $85$ frames?

When the time equaled $0$ seconds, the video had already played $190$ frames. The video had played $85$ *fewer* frames when the time equaled $-3\dfrac{2}{5}$ seconds.

$190-85=105$
The video had already played $105$ frames.

question.content:
Because of a problem in the program, the timer in a video player did not begin counting until the video had been playing for several seconds. The player began counting at $0$ seconds, even though the video had already played $190$ frames. The video plays $25$ frames per second.

**How many frames had the video already played when the time was equal to $-3\dfrac{2}{5}$ seconds?**

[[☃ numeric-input 1]] frames
